```sql
WITH lines AS (
    SELECT pv.product_id,
           ol.order_id,
           pv.id          AS variant_id,
           ol.quantity,
           ol.line_total_cents
      FROM order_lines ol
      JOIN orders o           ON o.id = ol.order_id
      JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.id = ol.variant_id::uuid
     WHERE o.tenant_id = %(tenant_id)s
       AND o.created_at >= %(from)s
       AND o.created_at <  %(to)s
       AND o.status IN ('paid', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered')
),
prod_totals AS (
    SELECT product_id,
           sum(quantity)         AS quantity,
           sum(line_total_cents) AS revenue_cents
      FROM lines
     GROUP BY product_id
),
prod_orders AS (
    SELECT product_id, count(*) AS order_count
      FROM (SELECT DISTINCT product_id, order_id FROM lines) d
     GROUP BY product_id
),
prod_variants AS (
    SELECT product_id, count(*) AS variant_count
      FROM (SELECT DISTINCT product_id, variant_id FROM lines) d
     GROUP BY product_id
)
SELECT p.id,
       p.sku,
       p.name,
       p.brand,
       p.currency,
       po.order_count,
       pt.quantity,
       pt.revenue_cents,
       pvc.variant_count
  FROM prod_totals pt
  JOIN prod_orders po    ON po.product_id  = pt.product_id
  JOIN prod_variants pvc ON pvc.product_id = pt.product_id
  JOIN products p        ON p.id = pt.product_id
 ORDER BY pt.quantity DESC, pt.revenue_cents DESC
 LIMIT %(limit)s
```

Uitleg: de `count(DISTINCT ...)`-aggregaten worden vervangen door twee kleinere `DISTINCT`-subquery's op (product, order) en (product, variant), zodat de sorteringen op de volledige regelset (~81k rijen) wegvallen en alleen de kleine productgroepen worden gesorteerd. Het verschil in snelheid is waarschijnlijk bescheiden, omdat de distincts nog steeds sorteren, maar de resultaten en volgorde blijven gelijk aan het origineel.
